Vulkan renders and presents directly (fastest). OpenGL ES shows the final frame through EGL, a compatibility path for devices with a broken Vulkan present path; falls back to Vulkan when unsupported. Applies from the next game start.

Mali only, with the Vulkan backend: run on a Vulkan 1.3 instance (the default) or a Vulkan 1.1 one. 1.1 helps Mali drivers whose 1.3 path misbehaves or that expose the required features only through extensions. Applies from the next game start.
Per axis: a 4K game at 50 % renders at 1080p (a quarter of the work). Lower resolution relieves the GPU; some games do not support it
Unreal Engine games render near 4K and are slow on mobile GPUs; used unless the game has its own setting
Avoids stutter; an object may take a moment to appear
Ring for CPU-updated data. Some games fill 64 MB every frame and wait on the GPU; a larger ring avoids that, but may cause visual glitches in a few titles
KB downloaded in one wait when a game reads GPU-written buffers page by page (one launch title\'s render thread). Larger can speed up sequential reads; too large wastes bandwidth on random access
Unreal titles poll completion with millions of spin-yields; after a burst a short sleep releases the core and the power budget. Off restores pure sched_yield (may help or hurt per title)
Detailed hot-path logging to logcat, for bug reports; slows the game while enabled
Submit to the GPU after every release event. Slower (a blocking submit per fence), but use if a game waits forever on a fence (stuck graphics after loading screens)
Imported Turnip (Adreno) or PanVK (Mali); System uses the vendor driver
Community Turnip (Adreno) or PanVK (Mali) builds; the one you install becomes the global driver

Keep the emulation and graphics threads on the fastest CPU cores (big.LITTLE).

Low latency keeps triple buffering (default); VSync paces to the display for the smoothest image; Uncapped presents every finished frame for the highest frame rate (may tear). Applies from the next game start.

Bandwidth-tuned defaults for Mali GPUs (same graphics): hardware render-target clears that keep AFBC compression alive, a 128 MB streaming buffer and one more pipeline worker. Auto applies it only on Mali GPUs; applies from the next game start.

Snapdragon-tuned defaults (same graphics): a 128 MB streaming buffer, one more shader-compile worker and an extra swapchain image for high-refresh presenting. Auto applies it only on Adreno GPUs; applies from the next game start.

Display mode and emulated vblank for games paced by vblank (same graphics): Auto follows the display’s highest rate, so 90/120 Hz screens stop capping games at 60 FPS; 60 keeps the previous behaviour. Applies from the next game start.

Fills idle display ticks with a generated in-between frame, so the presented image runs at the display rate. Real frames are untouched and still appear the moment they finish, so input response stays the same. On by default where the GPU has headroom (off on Mali and older Adreno chips); turn it on or off at will. Applies from the next game start.

Runs the game at half the working resolution with near-native picture quality: big textures are downscaled to 50% at upload and large render targets render at half size, resampled with an area-weighted filter so what you see stays at original quality while texture memory and bandwidth drop to a quarter - a large frame-rate gain on every device. Off by default; applies from the next game start.
Clear this game\'s overrides (options and GPU driver).
Lower the render scale while the game cannot hold its frame rate and raise it back when there is headroom. Applies without restarting.
